features: Important — This update changes the database: a migration adds two columns to the invoice coverages table (the link to the confirming transfer entry and the confirmation date). Run the migrations after updating.

Fund transfers (giroconti) — the Movements menu entry that was "under development" is now live. A transfer moves liquidity between the building's cash accounts: from the bank to a fund (setting money aside), from a fund to the bank (using it), or fund to fund. No real money moves — funds are accounting partitions of the single bank account — but every transfer is a double-entry record in the journal, with a GIR protocol number, a description and the ability to reverse it. The page lists all transfers with origin, destination and any linked coverage; the entry form shows each account's available balance and a preview of the journal entry before you confirm.

Reserve fund coverages can now actually be confirmed. When you record an invoice over budget with the "Reserve fund" strategy, the coverage is created as planned: from this version you confirm it with a transfer from the fund to the bank account — from the Transfers page or straight from the "Confirm with transfer" button shown on the invoice. On confirmation the fund is drawn down, the liquidity becomes available on the bank account again, and the invoice shows the protocol of the transfer covering it: from there you can proceed to payment through the normal flow. Reversing the transfer puts the coverage back to waiting, as before.

Important — The behaviour of overruns covered by a fund changes: recording the invoice no longer writes any accounting line on the fund. Previously the fund was moved immediately, before any confirmation; now it moves only when the confirming transfer is recorded. The overrun cost stays entirely on the expense line: the financial statement tells the truth, and the coverage is a financial fact tracked separately.

Important — Fixed the sign of fund balances. In three places the balance of a fund account was calculated with the convention inverted with respect to the rest of the system: depending on the page, the same fund could show opposite values. The formula is now the same everywhere (opening balance + inflows − outflows). If you have past invoices covered by a fund, the Transfers page will show a notice: the old entries need realigning with one click — the operation creates ordinary adjustment records in the journal, visible and reversible, without touching anything existing. The notice appears only if there is actually something to realign, and disappears by itself once done.

The treasury traffic light now singles out restricted liquidity. Money set aside in funds is no longer counted as available: if you have well-funded reserves you will see available liquidity drop and, in some cases, the light turn yellow. That is not a regression: it is the truth the calculation previously hid — a green light computed on restricted money was exactly the false positive this widget was built to eliminate.

Restricted funds (works, staff severance, arrears) cannot be drawn by a transfer without the assembly override already provided in the account's settings; transfers INTO a restricted fund remain always possible. No transfer can push the origin account below zero: the balance check always applies, with no exceptions. Reversals, on the other hand, are always allowed, as for every journal movement.

The coverage life cycle is guarded at every exit: an invoice whose coverage was confirmed by a transfer cannot be reversed or deleted while the transfer is alive — reverse the transfer first (the coverage goes back to waiting), then the invoice. Coverages of reversed invoices disappear from the confirmable list. An invoice with a fund coverage cannot be edited: the coverage is a snapshot of the overrun at recording time, and the way to change it is a reversal and a new entry.

The fund balance shown when recording an invoice is now net of coverages already promised and awaiting confirmation: previously two consecutive overruns could plan more against the same fund than it holds, and the impossibility only surfaced at confirmation time.

Three technical gaps closed: through direct calls (outside the interface) it was possible to collect an instalment into a fund, pay an invoice debiting a fund, or — by editing an existing payment — debit another building's account or a fund. Account type and ownership are now enforced server-side on every path.

For installers and support: the historical realignment is also available from the console with kondomanager:riallinea-fondi (with a --dry-run option to preview what would be adjusted without writing anything).

In-depth guides on the operational pages: invoice entry and Transfers now have a "Full guide" button opening a tabbed manual — like the one in the automation settings. The invoice guide covers every path of the form (prior-year debts, single-unit expenses, off-budget items, overruns and coverages); the transfers guide covers funds as partitions of the account, operations, confirmations and realignment. The overrun dialog texts were also updated: the "Reserve fund" strategy now clearly states the fund is drawn only upon confirmation by transfer.

Fixed a defect in invoice entry reported during testing: ticking "Prior-year debt" and then choosing the supplier made the prior-debt view disappear, replaced by the normal invoice view — the manual choice was wiped by an automatic date-based recalculation. The tick now survives supplier changes (the date automation stays: backdating the document still switches the view on by itself). Also, changing supplier kept the previously selected historical debt in the form, and the menu showed a raw number instead of its description: the selection is now cleared when the debt does not belong to the new supplier. Finally, when editing an invoice, its prior-year nature can no longer flip on screen by backdating the date.

Polish from testing on the Transfer and Immediate settlement forms: a "Save and new" button for batch entry (saves and reopens the empty form, no duplicate risk), "Back" and "Full guide" buttons on both pages, buttons aligned with the other forms, movements bar removed from both forms. Immediate settlement moves house: no longer a movements-bar entry but a button next to "New invoice" in the invoice list — it is the invoice's little sister, and now lives by its side. When only one financial year is open (the normal case), the year is no longer a menu but a simple statement. The pending-coverages card better explains its purpose, gets a dark look with a matching select, and the entry preview shows a balance seal that lights up when the entry is complete.
